classification.difficultyReason: Infer rectangle dimensions from tangencies, then subtract circle or semicircle areas to obtain each shaded region.

content.prompt: Find the approximate value of the shaded area for each of these figures. Use $\pi\approx3.14$.

spec.description: Circle tangent to all four sides of a square. The regions outside the circle are light purple. A marked centre and horizontal radius to the right boundary carry the supplied 12 mm label.
spec.mathematics: The circle radius is 12 mm; the square side equals the circle diameter.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied radius is labelled; inferred dimensions and areas remain hidden.

answer.worked:
The square's side equals the circle's diameter.
$$\begin{align*}s&=2\times12\\s&=24\text{ mm}\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=s^2-\pi r^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&\approx24^2-3.14\times12^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&\approx576-452.16\\A_{\text{shaded}}&\approx123.84\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two equal tangent circles lie side by side inside a rectangle, tangent to its top and bottom and corresponding outer ends. Both centres are marked. The rectangle height is labelled 4 m at the right. Light purple identifies the rectangle outside the circles.
spec.mathematics: Each diameter is 4 m, each radius is 2 m, and the rectangle width comprises two diameters.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 4 m height is labelled.

answer.worked:
Each circle has diameter $4\text{ m}$, and the rectangle is two diameters long.
$$\begin{align*}r&=4\div2\\r&=2\text{ m}\\l&=2\times4\\l&=8\text{ m}\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=l\times4-2\pi r^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&\approx8\times4-2\times3.14\times2^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&\approx32-25.12\\A_{\text{shaded}}&\approx6.88\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: An upper semicircle has its diameter along the entire bottom edge of a rectangle and touches the top edge. The diameter midpoint is marked and 70 mm is centred beneath the bottom edge. Light purple identifies the two regions outside the semicircle.
spec.mathematics: The diameter and rectangle width are 70 mm. The radius and rectangle height are half the diameter.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied diameter remains visible; calculated radius and areas are absent.

answer.worked:
The rectangle's height equals the semicircle's radius.
$$\begin{align*}r&=70\div2\\r&=35\text{ mm}\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=70r-\frac12\pi r^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&\approx70\times35-\frac12\times3.14\times35^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&\approx2450-1923.25\\A_{\text{shaded}}&\approx526.75\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upper semi-annulus with concentric arcs and a common horizontal baseline. The shorter sloping radius reaches the inner arc and is labelled 8 cm; the longer reaches the outer arc and is labelled 15 cm. Light purple identifies the semi-annulus.
spec.mathematics: Inner radius 8 cm and outer radius 15 cm. The required area is the difference between two semicircle areas.
spec.answerVisibility: Both supplied radii remain visible; no areas or calculated lengths are shown.

answer.worked:
Subtract the smaller semicircle's area from the larger semicircle's area.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{shaded}}&=\frac12\pi\times15^2-\frac12\pi\times8^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=\frac12\pi(225-64)\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=\frac{161\pi}{2}\\A_{\text{shaded}}&\approx\frac{161\times3.14}{2}\\A_{\text{shaded}}&\approx252.77\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
